hints: Because the load moves up the incline at constant speed, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), so the pulling force exerted by the winch balances the component of weight down the slope plus the resistance force.
Calculate the component of weight acting down the incline: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin 60^\circ = 50(10)\sin 60^\circ$.
Add the resistance force of $100\text{ N}$ to find the total pulling force of the winch, then use $W = F \times d$ with $d = 5\text{ m}$ to determine the work done.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane at constant speed ($a = 0$) with $m = 50\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$F_{\text{winch}} = mg\sin 60^\circ + 100 = 50(10)\sin 60^\circ + 100$$
$$F_{\text{winch}} = 500\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 100 = 250\sqrt{3} + 100 \approx 533.013\text{ N}$$

Calculate the work done by the winch force over a distance of $5\text{ m}$:
$$W = F_{\text{winch}} \times d = (250\sqrt{3} + 100) \times 5 = 1250\sqrt{3} + 500$$
$$W \approx 2165.06 + 500 = 2665.06\text{ J} \approx 2670\text{ J}$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work\u2013Energy Principle: Calculates total work done as $5(50g\sin 60^\circ + 100) = 2670\text{ J}$ (or $1250\sqrt{3} + 500\text{ J}$).
ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Resolves forces along the incline to find the tension force $F = 50g\sin 60^\circ + 100 = 533.0\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Identify the forces acting on the $50\text{ kg}$ load along the line of greatest slope of the $60^\circ$ inclined plane:
- Pulling force from the winch rope up the plane: $F$
- Component of gravity (weight) acting down the plane: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin 60^\circ$
- Resistance force acting down the plane opposing motion: $R = 100\text{ N}$

State Newton's second law along the plane for constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma = 0$$
$$F - mg\sin 60^\circ - R = 0$$
$$F = mg\sin 60^\circ + R$$
Substitute $m = 50\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $R = 100\text{ N}$:
$$F = (50)(10)\sin 60^\circ + 100 = 500\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 100 = 250\sqrt{3} + 100$$
Evaluate numerically:
$$F = 250(1.73205) + 100 = 433.013 + 100 = 533.013\text{ N}$$

State the formula for work done by a constant force along the displacement:
$$W = F \times d$$
Substitute $F = 250\sqrt{3} + 100\text{ N}$ and distance $d = 5\text{ m}$:
$$W = (250\sqrt{3} + 100)(5) = 1250\sqrt{3} + 500$$
Carry out the numerical multiplication:
$$W = 1250(1.73205) + 500 = 2165.06 + 500 = 2665.06\text{ J}$$
Rounding to three significant figures:
$$W = 2670\text{ J}$$
Thus the work done by the winch is $2670\text{ J}$.
